name: Sàn Art
watch: Vietnam premier independent artist-run space founded in 2007 by Dinh Q. Lê, Tuan Andrew Nguyen, and Phnam Thao Nguyen.
records_note: san-art.org has an expired certificate and was not opened; 2014 to 2018 coverage names a board chair but no annual report.

name: Tandanya National Aboriginal Cultural Institute
watch: Australia oldest Aboriginal-owned and governed multi-arts cultural centre, operating on Kaurna Yarta since 1989.

name: The Palestinian Museum
funding: Building (about US$24M, 2016) paid by 30-plus Palestinian families, Qattan Foundation, Bank of Palestine and the Arab Fund; Aliph funded a 2022 studio. No current donor list.
watch: Independent of Taawon since 2021. The claim that it takes no Palestinian Authority money has no source.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2020 to 2022, a named founding-donor list and eleven board directors; no separate audited accounts found.

name: Pinault Collection (Bourse de Commerce)
funding: Privately endowed by French luxury billionaire François Pinault (founder of Kering luxury conglomerate: Gucci, Saint Laurent, Balenciaga).
watch: Private luxury goods conglomerate prestige vehicle. Functions as a commercial brand-building showcase for Kering luxury holdings, receiving massive state tax deductions.

name: AlUla Arts & Cultural Oasis
funding: 100% state-funded by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia via the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU), chaired directly by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS).
watch: Direct authoritarian state mega-project and petro-state artwashing designed to burnish international prestige amid severe human rights suppression and political imprisonment.

name: Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC)
funding: Funded directly by Reliance Industries (India largest fossil fuel petrochemical, refining, and telecom conglomerate) under billionaire Mukesh Ambani.
watch: Billionaire petro-industrial conglomerate prestige vehicle; corporate dominance of public cultural space in Mumbai.

name: Dallas Museum of Art
funding: City of Dallas, trustees, donor circles and endowment. FY2025 corporate donors include Hunt Consolidated and Kosmos Energy; foundations include Meadows and CM Bass; the Getty Foundation gave $100,000 to $249,999.
watch: Kosmos Energy, a Dallas oil and gas producer, is a FY2025 corporate donor. The pin's Hamon note rested on an old naming gift only.
records_note: Posts annual reports for FY2021 to FY2025, audited financial statements, named donors and a yearly board announcement with the full trustee list.

name: MCA Denver
funding: Expenses $79.7M (FY2025, incl. capital); SCFD sales tax, City of Denver, Anschutz and Hamilton gifts.
watch: Board list not published online; verdict rests on corporate partner and gala sponsor roster. Liberty Global is telecom/media money.
why_flagged: Board list not published online; verdict rests on corporate partner and gala sponsor roster. Liberty Global is telecom/media money.
records_note: It posts annual reports covering FY17 to FY24, each with donors by gift level, a board list in the report, and Form 990s on ProPublica.

name: Portland Art Museum
funding: Expenses $27.7M (FY2025); Boyle (Columbia Sportswear), Blair, Meier, Miller and Gilmore foundations, Oregon Community Foundation, city arts tax.
watch: Pacific Power, a fossil-heavy utility. In Aug 2023 it disbanded its 40-year volunteer docent council for paid guides, which drew public criticism.
records_note: No narrative annual reports; audited accounts 2019 to 2025 and 990s are on its site, major sponsors are named undated, and trustees are listed.

name: National Portrait Gallery
watch: Refused Sackler £1M in 2019; BP award ended 2022.
why_flagged: Refused Sackler £1M in 2019; BP award ended 2022.
records_note: It posts annual reports with audited accounts for 2012-13 to 2023-24, thanks named supporters in the latest, and lists trustees with attendance in each.
